newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Intense meetings to reach Hebron deal.
newsitem.headline: Intense meetings to reach Hebron deal.

text.p: Israeli and Palestinian leaders held an intense series of meetings with U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross amid reports an agreement on Israeli redeployment from the West Bank town of Hebron had been all but signed.
Early on Tuesday Ross was in session with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, briefing him on a late-night meeting with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.
"They are discussing the various aspects of the Hebron accord," Netanyahu's office said. "At this stage nothing further has been scheduled."

On Monday evening, Palestinians said there could be a summit meeting between the two leaders within hours but later they said they did not expect such a meeting overnight. The two leaders had met secretly on Saturday night.
Israel radio said Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai told a parliamentary committee the Hebron deal was concluded and all but signed.

Palestinian officials have been saying that remaining disagreements holding up the signing are not about Hebron but over the handover of rural West Bank land to the Palestinians as stipulated in existing PLO-Israeli accords.
Israel's handover of most of Hebron has been delayed for 10 months over security concerns. The city holy to Jews and Moslems is home to 400 Jewish settlers and 120,000 Palestinians.

Jewish settler spokesman Moshe Ben-Zimra said of the emerging deal: "The agreement presented by the defence minister to the parliament is the first step in destroying the Jewish community of Hebron...Thousands of Arabs can attack the Jewish homes here."

Netanyahu's office declined to comment on media reports the prime minister had offered to complete Israel's redeployment in the West Bank in September 1999 -- two years later than the Palestinian interpretation of their accord with Israel.

Before the latest meeting with Netanyahu, Ross expressed optimism. "I remain hopeful we will see an agreement soon but I can't predict when," he told reporters after meeting Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in an office at the Church of the Nativity, the traditional birthplace of Jesus, in Palestinian-ruled Bethlehem.
"Both sides are making a real effort," Ross added.

Israel announced it was easing its closure on Palestinian territories, issuing permits to 50 more members of the Palestinian Authority to travel from the Gaza Strip to the West Bank in addition to 150 who already hold permits.
It also increased the number of entry permits for businessmen and for trucks entering from the Gaza Strip.
